```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
library(rvis)
```

`rvisPlot()` dispatches a chart request to a wrapper function. Set `type` to
the chart method and `plotter` to the wrapper prefix, then pass the data and
the dimension mappings that the chart needs.

```{r bar-example, eval=FALSE}
species <- aggregate(Petal.Length ~ Species, data = iris, FUN = mean)

rvisPlot(
  type = "bar",
  plotter = "amCharts",
  obj = species,
  x = "Species",
  y = "Petal.Length",
  config = list(title = "Mean petal length by species")
)
```

The same input and dimension mappings can be sent to other wrappers that
implement `bar`, such as `billboarder`, `c3`, `googleVis`, `highcharter`, or
`plotly`. Each wrapper has its own configuration options and may impose
additional data requirements. The [chart type manual](chart-types.html) lists
the exact wrapper methods and their arguments.

Examples of every chart type with each of its plotters are in the chart guides:
[comparing categories](comparing-categories.html),
[parts of a whole](parts-of-a-whole.html),
[relationships and distributions](relationships-distributions.html),
[time series](time-series.html),
[networks and hierarchies](networks-hierarchies.html) and
[tables](tables.html).

## Dimension arguments

Dimension arguments such as `x`, `y`, `label`, and `theta` refer to columns in
`obj`. Use a character column name for a single field. Use a named list when
the wrapper supports multiple series and the series need distinct names, for
example `y = list(actual = "actual", forecast = "forecast")`.

```{r timeseries-example, eval=FALSE}
series <- data.frame(
  date = as.POSIXct("2025-01-01", tz = "UTC") + (0:11) * 86400,
  actual = 30 + sin((0:11) * pi / 6) * 5,
  forecast = 31 + sin((0:11) * pi / 6) * 4
)

rvisPlot(
  type = "tsline",
  plotter = "amCharts",
  obj = series,
  x = "date",
  y = list(actual = "actual", forecast = "forecast"),
  config = list(title = "Actual and forecast")
)
```

## Configuration

Supply wrapper settings through `config`, a named list. Common settings include
titles, axes, legends, colors, and layout options. Configuration keys are
wrapper-specific: consult the [configuration reference](configuration.html)
for the accepted type, default, and valid values of every key recorded by the
package. Extra `...` arguments are forwarded to the underlying chart
constructor where the wrapper supports them.

## Choosing a wrapper

The wrappers are optional dependencies. Install the plotting package for the
wrapper you plan to use. Then change `plotter` while keeping the chart type,
data, and mappings when both wrappers implement the same chart. The package's
chart type index shows which exact methods are available.
